rules.title: Empty block has type ()
rules.statement: A block expression `{}` with no statements evaluates to the unit/void type `()`.

rules.title: Block value is its trailing tail expression
rules.statement: The type and value of a block `{ s1; ...; e }` are those of its final element when that element is a tail/expression statement (or a non-statement expression form); a block whose final element is a `let`, destructuring-let, `return`, or `;`-terminated expr-stmt produces no tail value and types as `()`.

rules.title: Block with diverging tail call types as !
rules.statement: If a block's final tail expression is a call to a `-> !` (diverging) callee, the block types as the never type `!`; the diverging call is still emitted and the block contributes no concrete value type to its context.

rules.title: Block ending in `return e` adopts e's type
rules.statement: A block whose final statement is `return e` is non-diverging in the value system: the block's result type is taken as `typeof(e)` even though no value is produced, so the divergent block is usable at a non-void expected type (e.g. inside a tuple/struct literal). The `return` is still lowered and executed.
rules.divergence: No real `!`/never subtyping for tail-return; the return-value's type is adopted as a block-type proxy instead of `!`.
rules.uncertainty: Behavior is a stated workaround pending full never-type support.

rules.title: if/if-let in expression position requires else
rules.statement: An `if` or `if let` used as an expression (yielding a value) must have an `else` branch; an `if` without `else` is only valid in statement position.

rules.title: if condition must be bool
rules.statement: The condition of a non-`let` `if` must have type `bool`; the error/never types are also accepted (error recovery and diverging conditions).

rules.title: if-let expression lowers to a two-arm match
rules.statement: `if let P = e { THEN } else { ELSE }` in expression position is equivalent to `match e { P => THEN, _ => ELSE }`; the pattern's bindings are in scope only within THEN, and the result type is that of the THEN branch.

rules.title: if-expr branches must have compatible types
rules.statement: In an `if` expression, the THEN and ELSE branch types must be mutually compatible (one assignable to the other); incompatible non-error, non-never branch types are an error. The result type is the unification (LUB) of the two branch types.

rules.title: Never/error branch yields the other branch's type
rules.statement: A branch typed `!` (never) or error contributes no type to an `if` expression: the expression's type is the other branch's type. `!` behaves as a subtype of every type at the join. A branch whose final statement is `return`/`break`/`continue` (or a diverging tail call) is typed `!`.

rules.title: Two fn-item branches join to a fn pointer
rules.statement: When both `if` branches are distinct fn-item values with the same signature, the result type is the corresponding fn-pointer type `fn(params)->ret` (fn-item-to-fn-pointer coercion at the join), since two distinct fn-items are not directly type-compatible.

rules.title: Integer-literal if-result widens to i64 on i32 overflow
rules.statement: If an `if` expression's result type is an unresolved integer literal and either branch's literal value exceeds the i32 range, the result type is i64.

rules.title: if-let chain requires at least two segments
rules.statement: An `if let ... && ...` chain must contain at least two segments (let-bindings and/or conditions); fewer is an error. The chain desugars inside-out into nested `if let`/`if` with the `else` branch duplicated at each fall-through.
rules.uncertainty: ELSE duplication at each fall-through is documented as an accepted limitation, not a fundamental rule.

rules.title: Closure type hint derived from a Fn-family type-param bound
rules.statement: When the expected type is a type parameter bounded by an Fn-family trait (Fn/FnMut/FnOnce(params)->ret), a closure literal in that position is given the inferred closure type with parameter and return types taken from the bound (after generic substitution).
